clue.text: Appease China, covering up one thing oddly

indicators.note: to cover something up is to wrap round it, so the friend's word goes outside the rest

parts.note: rhyming slang: china plate means mate, a friend
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in the odd positions of the word before it

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of thing

explanation.surface: Someone placating China by concealing one item in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: China with a capital C looks like the country, but it is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To mitigate is to soften or pacify, a close synonym of appease in the sense of easing anger or severity.

clue.text: Dispute expected fine being raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the letters means reading them from the bottom up

parts.note: due means expected, as in a train due at noon
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: An argument over an anticipated penalty that has gone up.
explanation.walkthrough: DUE plus F is DUEF, which read upwards becomes FEUD.
explanation.definitionFit: A feud is a long-running quarrel, so it serves as a noun synonym for a dispute.

clue.text: Closure of branches over Welsh banker's county

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its final letter, the point where it ends

parts.note: the last letter of branches
the Taff is a river in South Wales, and a banker is a river (it has banks); with the apostrophe s

explanation.surface: Pruning trees beyond the county home of a bank employee from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Banker looks like someone who works in a bank, but in crosswords it is a river, here the Taff in Cardiff. In a down clue, over puts S on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffs is the standard abbreviation for Staffordshire, an English county in the Midlands.

clue.text: Promote at college holder of degree, first in English

parts.note: a student who is up is in residence at university
a grad is a graduate, someone holding a degree

indicators.note: first in points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of English

explanation.surface: Advancing a graduate at a university, with English being their first subject.
explanation.walkthrough: Being up at college is British usage for studying at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To upgrade someone is to raise them to a higher grade or rank, so it matches promote as a verb.

clue.text: Recalled performing popular parts for pantomime

indicators.note: to part something is to split it, so this word pushes into the middle of the jumble
performing suggests working letters into a fresh act, so the word before is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: An actor called back to play favourite roles in a Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: Parts looks like acting roles, but it means splits: the shuffled letters are divided after their first letter. A pantomime is a British family stage show at Christmas based on a fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinderella is one of the best-loved pantomime stories, so the title names a whole pantomime as an example.

clue.text: A lot of bubbly males protecting a wildebeest

indicators.note: something protecting another surrounds it, so the outer letters go round the inner ones

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male, and two of them make the plural
taken as written
the gnu is another name for the wildebeest

explanation.surface: Plenty of excited bulls guarding a single antelope on the savannah.
explanation.walkthrough: Bubbly looks like a description of the males, but it is slang for champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a large wine bottle holding two standard bottles, so it is a lot of champagne.

clue.text: Avoid sleep regularly? That is to stop!

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so one piece fills the middle of another
regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one here

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of sleep
id est is the Latin for that is, usually shortened to i.e.

explanation.surface: Advice to dodge sleep now and then, ending with a firm call to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: That is normally gives IE; here it is the full Latin ID EST, which sits inside S-EP.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep a problem is to evade it by stepping aside, a figurative synonym of avoid.

clue.text: Reportedly something groom may hold arriving at wedding

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the sound of the word matters, not its spelling

parts.note: a groom who tends horses holds the bridle, the headgear and reins

explanation.surface: A bridegroom carrying something as he turns up at his marriage ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: The groom is not the bridegroom but a stable hand, who holds a horse's bridle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal and wedding both work as adjectives for the marriage ceremony, as in bridal or wedding party.

clue.text: Spirit cook mostly added to make sweet bread

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: brio is liveliness or spirit
a chef is a cook

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a dash of liquor goes in, and the baker produces a sweet loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit suggests alcohol in a kitchen scene, but it is vigour, BRIO; CHEF loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Brioche is a soft French bread enriched with butter, eggs and sugar, so a sweet bread.

clue.text: German child, helpful type

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the German word for child, as in kindergarten
third meaning: a sort or variety

explanation.surface: A young German who is an obliging sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: Helpful type reads as one phrase about a person, but helpful and type are separate meanings, giving three in all.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is German for a child, an English adjective for considerate, and an English noun for a sort.

clue.text: Sinister reason to attend an auction?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: threatening and unfriendly in appearance
second meaning, read as two words: you go to a sale for the purpose of making offers

explanation.surface: Is there something menacing about turning up to a saleroom?
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as FOR BIDDING: that is why one attends an auction.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbidding describes something grim and threatening in look, which is close to sinister.

clue.text: French port controversial actor knocked back somewhat

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so the letters run the other way
somewhat means only part of the words, so a run of letters is taken from inside them

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A disputed performer gets a partial rebuff at a Channel ferry town.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, the run of letters from controversial actor gives CALAIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Calais is the northern French port facing Dover, the main crossing point on the Channel.

clue.text: Scholarly American appearing on acclaimed broadcast

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A learned US guest on a well-reviewed radio or TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, appearing on puts A above the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Academical is an older adjective form of academic, meaning relating to learning and scholarship.

clue.text: Grace last month heading for obscure Scottish island

parts.note: December is the last month of the year, abbreviated

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of obscure
Rum is one of the Small Isles of the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: Someone called Grace who, a month ago, was bound for a remote Hebridean isle.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace with a capital letter poses as a name; it is the quality of good manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is seemly, polite behaviour, which overlaps with grace in the sense of courteous propriety.

clue.text: Spell in the past having essentially slender figure

parts.note: a hex is a curse or magic spell
ago means in the past, as in years ago

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the very centre of the word that follows

parts.note: the central letter of slender

explanation.surface: A charm once cast that gave someone a slim body.
explanation.walkthrough: Figure looks like a body shape to go with slender, but it is a geometric figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A hexagon is a six-sided plane shape, an example of a figure in geometry.

clue.text: Is a poet mixed up in drugs?

indicators.note: mixed up means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about whether a confused writer of verse is dabbling in narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the many poets, such as Coleridge, who used opium.
explanation.definitionFit: Opiates are narcotics derived from opium, such as morphine, so they are a class of drugs.

clue.text: Plant, one in second row at rear of border

parts.note: a hem is the edge or border of cloth
in rugby, a lock is a forward who plays in the second row of the scrum

explanation.surface: A garden plant, one of a second line placed at the back of a flowerbed.
explanation.walkthrough: The scene is a herbaceous border, but second row is a rugby position: the lock forwards pack down in the scrum's second row.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemlock is a poisonous plant of the carrot family, the one said to have killed Socrates.

clue.text: Crowd around black dog that's slipped its lead

indicators.note: slipping its lead means losing the front, so the first letter goes

parts.note: ca is short for circa, Latin for around
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
a poodle is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: People gather round a dark-coated dog that has escaped from its leash.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead suggests a dog lead; here it means the leading letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Caboodle means a group or lot of people or things, best known in the phrase the whole caboodle.

clue.text: Secret, why possibly it's overheard

definitions.meaning: first meaning: not known to others
second meaning: spoken, the word why sounds like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Something hush-hush, which is perhaps why someone eavesdropped.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra, letters such as x and y stand for unknowns; the word why, said out loud, is the letter y.
explanation.definitionFit: Unknown means not known or kept hidden, so it matches secret as an adjective; in maths it is a noun for a variable.

clue.text: Not large, West African peninsula

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; it names the peninsula in the phrase Iberian Peninsula

indicators.note: not large tells the solver to remove the abbreviation for large

parts.note: a Liberian comes from Liberia in West Africa
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A small West African stretch of coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: LIBERIAN loses its L to leave IBERIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian Peninsula holds Spain and Portugal, so Iberian is the word that identifies that peninsula.

clue.text: Disregard piece from reporter on Gibraltar coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read from the bottom upwards
a piece from the words is a portion of them, so the letters are inside

parts.note: the letters bridging the three words

explanation.surface: Pay no attention to an article by a journalist about the Rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Piece suggests a newspaper article by the reporter; it signals a run of letters, which read upwards give IGNORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to pay it no heed, a direct verb synonym of disregard.

clue.text: Rejected urge to ring supporter not far away

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters run the opposite way
to ring something is to encircle it, so one word goes round another

parts.note: a yen is a longing or urge
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A spurned desire to phone a fan who lives close by.
explanation.walkthrough: Supporter looks like a fan, but in crosswords it is often an undergarment. The container is built first, and then the whole is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearby means close at hand, so it is a straight equivalent of not far away.

clue.text: Becoming aware of love, ditching husband!

indicators.note: ditching means getting rid of, so a letter is removed

parts.note: love is a score of nothing in tennis
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Realising one is in love after leaving a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Love here is the tennis score zero, NOTHING, which loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting means observing or registering something, so it fits becoming aware of as a present participle.

clue.text: Charge to hold criminal isn't vague

indicators.note: to hold something is to contain it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to indict is to charge formally with a crime

indicators.note: criminal means crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A prosecutor admits the charge to hold the suspect is not woolly.
explanation.walkthrough: Criminal looks like the person held, but it is the anagram signal on the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Indistinct means not clearly seen or heard, an adjective synonym of vague.

clue.text: Shine in golf of inferior standard

parts.note: golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet
low means poor or of inferior quality

explanation.surface: A poor golfer still manages to excel.
explanation.definitionFit: A glow is a steady light or radiance, close to shine as a noun.

clue.text: Innate quality that's present

definitions.meaning: second meaning: something given to someone

explanation.surface: A natural characteristic that is there in someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Present reads as an adjective meaning there, but it is a noun for something given.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an inborn talent and a thing handed over freely, matching each phrase.

clue.text: Ways to reach National Park?

parts.note: surface reading: routes for getting to a protected area of countryside
setter's reading: wide ways, the plural of an adjective for wide plus a word for routes, which together name a Norfolk National Park

explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk and Suffolk Broads, a network of shallow lakes and rivers in eastern England, has national park status; the answer also reads as wide ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The Broads is the name of the wetland National Park in East Anglia, and broad ways would be ways to reach it.

clue.text: Surprising financial gain damaged Apple, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: unexpected money, such as a legacy
second meaning: fruit blown off a tree by the wind, often bruised

explanation.surface: An unexpected profit for a struggling tech giant with a capital A.
explanation.walkthrough: Apple with a capital looks like the technology company, but it is just the fruit, bruised from falling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an unexpected sum of money and fruit brought down by the wind.
